title: Non-CSS Quantum Code Embedding
abstract: We generalize the unified framework in [Phys. Rev. A 113, 022438 (2026)] to accommodate arbitrary stabilizer codes (referred as non-CSS for emphasis). The generalization has immediate consequences in areas including logical measurement, quantum weight reduction and Euclidean embedding. For example, currently CSS (pure $X,Z$-type) logical measurements are well-understood based on the (height-1) cone, while non-CSS (e.g., $Y$-type) logical measurements are ad hoc (e.g., rely on local Clifford transform). Similarly, quantum weight reduction and optimal Euclidean embeddings only exist for CSS input codes. Here, we show that our generalized framework addresses this issue, and thus many constructions, including qLDPC surgery, Layer Codes and quantum weight reduction generalize to non-CSS codes in a relatively straightforward fashion. The previously mentioned examples are derived in detail for clarity.
summary: This paper generalizes the mathematical framework for quantum error correction from restricted CSS codes to arbitrary non-CSS stabilizer codes. By employing symplectic complexes, the authors show that crucial techniques like logical measurement and code embedding can be extended to these more general, physically relevant codes. This significantly broadens the theoretical toolkit for designing fault-tolerant quantum computation.
main_problem: The paper generalizes the framework for quantum code embedding from being restricted to Calderbank–Shor–Steane (CSS) codes to accommodate arbitrary stabilizer codes (non-CSS).
main_result: A generalized algebraic framework, utilizing symplectic complexes, successfully extends constructions like logical measurement, quantum weight reduction, and Euclidean embedding to non-CSS codes in a straightforward manner.
method: The authors develop and apply a generalized algebraic framework based on symplectic complexes and the analysis of the height-2 cone to unify various quantum error correction procedures.
model_or_system: The study focuses on quantum error correcting codes, specifically stabilizer codes, encompassing both CSS and general non-CSS types (e.g., those involving Y-type logical measurements).
key_observables: Logical measurement outcomes (X-type vs. Y-type), quantum weight reduction metrics, and the structure of the symplectic embedding.
important_parameters: The number of qubits ($n$), the maximum check weight ($w$), and the structure of the underlying symplectic forms over F2.
main_assumptions: Previous work was limited to CSS codes; the generalization relies on the properties of the height-2 cone within the symplectic setting.
figures_summary: Table I compares CSS-only restrictions versus non-CSS generalizations across key diagnostics. Table II compares specific constructions like Layer Codes for CSS vs. Non-CSS cases.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the limitations of CSS-only methods to introducing the generalized symplectic framework (Theorem 2), and finally detailing complex procedures for non-CSS logical measurement and fast surgery (Algorithms 10 & 11).
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, unified mathematical language (symplectic geometry) to analyze quantum error correction beyond the well-understood CSS regime, which is crucial for realizing complex quantum hardware.
